title: Octameric dGTPase assemblies mediate broad anti-phage defense
task: Characterize dGTPase oligomerization and antiviral mechanism
key_results: Octameric Vibrio dGTPase assemblies are essential and sufficient for antiviral activity; cryo-EM resolved octamer, 16-mer, and filamentous forms; dAMP identified as allosteric regulator
comments: The finding that higher-order assemblies are dispensable for function suggests oligomerization stoichiometry is tightly tuned for immune defense.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Octamer formation is required for antiviral defense activity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—octamers are essential and sufficient for antiviral activity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher-order oligomeric assemblies enhance antiviral function
hypotheses.result: Rejected—16-mer and filamentous forms are dispensable for activity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nucleotide allosteric regulation modulates dGTPase function
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—dAMP acts as an allosteric regulator

title: Resolving FRET signal degeneracy and population heterogeneity via Bayesian nonparametrics
task: Infer molecular states from FRET data with heterogeneous populations
key_results: BNP-FRET-Bin framework eliminates need for user-predefined state numbers; distinguishes kinetically-distinct states with overlapping FRET efficiencies; provides uncertainty estimates for kinetic rates and state identities
comments: The Bayesian nonparametric approach elegantly addresses a fundamental limitation of FRET—signal degeneracy from projection of 3D conformations to 1D measurements—enabling inference from kinetic signatures alone.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Kinetic signatures distinguish states with overlapping FRET efficiencies
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—BNP-FRET-Bin identifies distinct configurations via kinetic differences despite identical FRET signals

hypotheses.hypothesis: User-predefinition of state number and noise characteristics is necessary for accurate FRET analysis
hypotheses.result: Rejected—BNP-FRET-Bin achieves accurate inference with minimal user-tuned parameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Population heterogeneity and molecule-to-molecule variability can be resolved from single FRET traces
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—framework enables simultaneous high-throughput analysis of biologically heterogeneous populations

title: Thioredoxin interacting protein (TXNIP), a redox regulator, mediates the EPAC-RAP1 signaling dependency of primary melanoma
task: Identify TXNIP as downstream effector of EPAC-RAP1 signaling controlling redox homeostasis in primary melanoma growth and metastatic progression
key_results: EPAC inhibition or genetic deletion reduces melanomagenesis in Braf/Pten mice; low EPAC and RAP1-GTP expression correlate with better recurrence-free survival; EPAC activation upregulates TXNIP via mTORC1–HIF-1α axis to promote redox homeostasis and mitochondrial ROS regulation; TXNIP acts as critical downstream effector of EPAC signaling
comments: The identification of TXNIP as a key EPAC effector controlling metabolic adaptation and redox balance in primary melanoma provides mechanistic rationale for targeting EPAC-dependency; however, the transition from primary to metastatic disease involves loss of this dependency, meriting investigation of alternative pathways.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Loss of EPAC dependency during metastatic progression requires bypass mechanisms
